body: ### Problem A line containing U+2028 (LINE SEPARATOR) produces stale or duplicated characters when Neovim scrolls horizontally. **Additional context**: I initially reported this to Ghostty: https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/discussions/14821 A Ghostty collaborator identified a width disagreement: Ghostty treats U+2028 as width 0, while Neovim treats it as width 1. They suggested that Neovim might classify it as non-printable: https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/discussions/14821#discussioncomment-19157453 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Run `nvim --clean`. 2. Set `:set nowrap`. 3. Resize the terminal to 120 columns. 4. Enter Insert mode and paste the following text. It contains an actual U+2028 immediately before the second group of words: ```text xxxx xxx xxxxxx xxx xxxxxxx xxxx xx+ xxxxx xx xxxxx.  xxx xxxx xxxxxxx xxxxxxx xxxxx, xxx xxx xx xx xxx xxxxx xxxxxxx xxxxxxx xx xxxxxx.² ``` 5. Type `"` at the end and press Escape. Ghost characters can appear near the end of the line, including apparent copies of `²` or other stale glyphs. The window width matters: the issue does not reproduce at every width. Replacing U+2028 with an ordinary space prevents the issue in my tests. ### Expected behavior The displayed text should remain correct during horizontal scrolling, without stale or duplicated glyphs. ### Nvim version (nvim -v) 0.12.6 ### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same? seems less frequent in vim, v9.1 ### Operating system/version 26.6.2 ### Terminal name/version ghostty 1.3..1 ### $TERM environment variable xterm-ghostty ### Installation homebrew
title: Display corruption when horizontally scrolling a line containing U+2028
